summary.tldr: Lowers the voting age in federal elections and referendums from 18 to 16, and updates related rules to match.
what_it_does: Lowers the voting age for Canadian citizens in federal elections from 18 to 16.
Changes the definition of “future elector” to mean a Canadian citizen who is 14 or 15 years old.
Removes the rule that election officers appointed under section 32 may be under 18 but must be at least 16.
Updates election offence and declaration rules so they refer to people who are under 16, not under 18.
Applies the same 16-year-old voting age to referendums under the related regulation.
Sets the law to start six months after royal assent, unless the Chief Electoral Officer says sooner that preparations are ready.
summary.background: The bill amends the Canada Elections Act and a related referendum regulation.
